sources.title: High levels of population genetic differentiation in the American crocodile (Crocodylus acutus)
sources.scope: Population-genetic analysis across continental America and the Greater Antilles using mitochondrial control-region sequences and 11 nuclear microsatellite loci; new samples from five countries plus public sequences.
sources.license: CC0 public-domain dedication, stated in the article copyright section.
sources.rightsEvidenceLocator: Copyright statement after article citation; CC0 public-domain dedication.
sources.attribution: Rossi NA, Menchaca-Rodriguez A, Antelo R, Wilson B, McLaren K, Mazzotti F, et al. (2020). High levels of population genetic differentiation in the American crocodile (Crocodylus acutus). PLoS ONE 15(7):e0235288. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0235288. Claims are paraphrased.

claims.text: The study found strong genetic differentiation among sampled American-crocodile localities, especially between continental and Greater Antillean samples, and reported three newly identified haplotypes in Venezuelan samples.
claims.scope: Genetic markers and sampled localities only; not a population census or abundance estimate.

gaps: No multi-source species dossier is added.
